notes:
Quarantine status: clone made into a new empty folder (ingest/tokeneconomizer/src) with core.hooksPath=/dev/null and core.symlinks=false. Nothing was installed, built, or run from the repo. The only things executed were curl against the GitHub REST API, git clone/rev-parse/log/ls-files, and read-only cat/grep/sed. One Python metadata parser was run with -I from a separate folder: tools_te/meta.py. The raw API responses are saved in that tools_te folder. The OAW reference was not touched. No Dockerfile, no .mcp.json or MCP server definition, and no curl|sh or npx installer were found.

What it is: a multi-host agent plugin for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Cursor, Pi and opencode. Its description is "Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents" (Microsoft + Berkeley). It has three mechanisms:
1. micro-skills: short repository facts distilled from finished session transcripts and injected at SessionStart. Default is off.
2. toolprune: removes tools a repository's sessions never use. Default is auto.
3. loopguard: detects a turn stuck in a failure loop and nudges it. Default is nudge.
An optional repomap (default off) generates an aider-style token-budgeted repo map through the optional aider-chat extra. It is not an embedding or vector store.

Integration surface:
- Claude Code hooks.json registers one launcher, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/te-hook, on SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop and SessionEnd, with timeouts of 10-60s. Codex, Copilot and Cursor get equivalent hook files. The Codex file has a Windows variant that runs python -c with runpy.
- te-hook is a POSIX sh script that finds python3/python/py and runs te_bootstrap.py hook.
- Install per README: git clone, then `claude plugin marketplace add`, then `claude plugin install tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer`. Pi installs with `pi install git:github.com/microsoft/TokenEconomizer`.
- The Python package declares no dependencies (dependencies=[]). Optional extras: test (pytest) and baselines (aider-chat).

Side effects that matter for an OAW safety review (all from reading the code; none was run):
(a) It keeps state in ~/.tokeneconomizer (or $TOKENECONOMIZER_HOME). At every session start it writes a launcher, ~/.tokeneconomizer/bin/te (paths.ensure_launcher).
(b) toolprune defaults to 'auto'. It writes permissions.deny entries into the project's .claude/settings.local.json; for Codex it writes .codex/config.toml toggles, and for Copilot .github/copilot/settings.local.json disabledMcpServers. It adds the files it creates to .git/info/exclude. This is persistent configuration change made without asking per change.
(c) Side calls run the user's own agent CLI as a subprocess, for example `claude -p --tools "" --max-turns 1` on haiku, or `codex exec`, `copilot -p`, `opencode run`, `pi --print`. These are billed to the user's account, and TE_SIDECALL=1 is set so the nested agent does not trigger the hooks again.
(d) Hooks start detached background processes (context.spawn, winspawn on Windows) for folding sessions, the judge, and the repo map.
(e) It reads agent session transcripts, plus ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.copilot/hooks/*.json (to detect rtk), and ~/.codex and ~/.copilot state.

experiments/ (77 files) is benchmark-only and is excluded from the package. It holds Docker-based SWE-bench and Web-Bench harnesses and launch shell scripts. tests/ has 29 offline pytest files, including test_live_hooks.py.

A grep of the markdown found no prompt-injection-style text. CLAUDE.md is ordinary contributor guidance and was treated as data.

Fit with the user's request: TokenEconomizer is a token and cost control layer, not a knowledge map or vectorization tool. It does not overlap with replacing an LLM wiki, except loosely through micro-skills (learned per-repository facts) and the optional repomap. claude-mem and graphify were not part of this scouting task.

Smaller points: the git symlink plugin/lib/tokeneconomizer was checked out as a plain-text file because of core.symlinks=false. The languages list comes from counting file extensions in the clone, because the /languages API was not among the calls requested.
